explanation: Measure the area at the two ends and move the shorter wall inward. Keeping that shorter wall while narrowing the gap cannot improve the area.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n heights. Each iteration moves one boundary inward, so there are at most n-1 iterations.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. Only the two indices and best area are retained.
attribution: Original repository-authored Blind75 JavaScript algorithm, promoted from the validated correct fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: The shorter of two boundary heights limits the current area. Keeping that boundary while moving only the other boundary inward cannot improve either width or limiting height. Discarding the shorter boundary is therefore safe, and the two-pointer scan cannot discard every optimal pair before considering it.
walkthrough: For heights [2,7,4,6], the outer pair has area 3×2=6. Move past height 2; heights 7 and 6 are two positions apart and give area 2×6=12. The remaining narrower choices cannot exceed 12, so return 12.
edgeCases: Exactly two heights define the container.
